niches.label: MVA / Personal Injury
niches.intro: Competitor MVA ads from the Meta Ad Library (US, active), picked from the top results by impressions. Green 'Iterate for us' lines are Case Source test ideas.

niches.label: Moving
niches.intro: Competitor long-distance moving ads from the Meta Ad Library (US, active), picked from the top results by impressions. Our own VAM ads are left out. Green lines are VAM/NSR test ideas.

ads.breakdown: 3D anatomy renders (glowing neck and spine, a woman holding her neck) cut with phone footage of real wrecks and redacted check close-ups. Orange karaoke captions. Ends on a screen recording of the quiz.
ads.iterate: 3D whiplash explainer for our crash-type angle: show the injury, not a cartoon.

ads.breakdown: Opens on a CGI driver, then a stock-photo slideshow (doctor, paperwork, phone call) with one word on screen at a time. Ends on an animated 'Evaluating your accident… Step 6 of 6' app screen.
ads.iterate: Animated 'evaluating your claim' end card on our AI UGC.

ads.breakdown: TikTok comment-bubble hook ('someone hit me yesterday, my neck's killing me and I have no clue what to even do'), stock clips with kinetic words, animated '$20k–$200k+ · people checked today' card.
ads.iterate: Comment-reply opener on a 3 Reasons Why video.

ads.breakdown: Couch UGC with a yellow hook bar that stays on screen the whole time ('He almost took $7,500. He was owed $112,000.'). Cuts to an animated phone quiz over a blurred background, then a money-rain end card.
ads.iterate: Persistent hook bar + phone-mockup quiz on our Premature Settlement Risk UGC.

ads.breakdown: Creator green-screened over b-roll of other people's check reveals, a shocked reaction, a settlement letter, then a quiz screen. Cheap to make: one talking-head take plus stitched b-roll.
ads.iterate: Green-screen storytime reusing our existing b-roll library.

ads.breakdown: Larry H. Parker: phone quiz mockup on yellow, countdown timer, arrows pointing to 'Learn More', '100K clients helped' motion graphic.
ads.iterate: 10s cut that is only the animated quiz + one hook line.

ads.breakdown: Creator at a podcast mic, screen recording of someone typing into the form, money b-roll, highlighted word captions. Closest MVA example of the playbook's podcast style.
ads.iterate: Podcast-style AI UGC (two people or solo mic).

ads.breakdown: Mailbox POV skit: 'POV you tried to get that car accident check (spoiler: I got 45k)'. Sad face at the mailbox, envelope, check to camera, then talks to camera.
ads.iterate: We already run a mailbox ad; test new avatars and settings so Meta sees it as a new ad. Counsel check on dollar results.

ads.breakdown: Orange top third with '⚠️ The insurance company hopes you don't know THIS after a CAR CRASH' stays on screen the whole video. Man rants underneath with green word captions.
ads.iterate: Split-screen header on a long-form 3 Reasons Why.

ads.breakdown: Polished presenter, crash-type hook 'WERE YOU REAR-ENDED RECENTLY?' Injuryfaqs runs one version per crash type.
ads.iterate: Crash-type series: rear-ended, T-boned, rideshare.

ads.breakdown: Same Injuryfaqs template, T-boned version: 'Side-impact crashes often lead to neck, back, and shoulder injuries.'
ads.iterate: Crash-type series: rear-ended, T-boned, rideshare.

ads.breakdown: Dramatized crash-scene skit (two drivers arguing, 'someone rear ended…'). Long copy with one specific dollar story ($4,200 offer → $80,000). Headline: 'Find Out If You Qualify For A Second, Bigger Check.'
ads.iterate: Swap our '30–70% lower' line for one real before/after number (needs a real client example).

ads.breakdown: Settlement Claim Connect: in-car UGC ('a clock' — deadline angle) with 'TEXAS CAR ACCIDENT CLAIMS' and a ✅ checklist in copy (Texas, last 6 months, no attorney yet). Running TX and GA versions since 9/17.
ads.iterate: State callouts for GA/IL/TX/AL with our MQL rules as the checklist.

ads.breakdown: Settlement Claim Connect, launched 9/28: 'Their insurance paid for your totaled car. That check covers the car. It doesn't cover what the crash cost you.'
ads.iterate: 'The car check isn't your claim' angle for people who think it's already settled.

ads.breakdown: Jacoby & Meyers 17s: 'Hurt in a car accident?' over an LA street stock clip. Bernard Law Group runs the same clip, so it's likely a shared vendor template.
ads.iterate: Ultra-short 10–15s cut of our strongest hook.

ads.breakdown: Bernard Law Group: same stock clip and copy template as other firms ('Most accident victims never get the compensation they deserve… Take this free quiz').
Wreck photo with 'GET 3X MORE FROM YOUR CAR ACCIDENT CLAIM' and a payout-range list by crash type (T-bone, sideswipe, head-on, rollover, hit and run).
ads.iterate: Static: payout ranges by crash type (needs real, approved numbers; keep 'may').

ads.breakdown: Settlement receipts list: '$21,400 — Rear-end collision / $39,200 — T-bone accident / $16,750 — Minor injury claim / See If You Qualify'.
ads.iterate: Receipts static by crash type (needs real, approved numbers).

ads.breakdown: 1:41 long-form. Screen recording of the form ('Can you quickly explain what happened?') with the keyboard up. Broad qualifier: any vehicle accident in the last 12 months.

ads.advertiser: Law Offices of Gary Martin Hays & Associates, P.C.
ads.breakdown: Georgia firm, running since Oct 2024: 'Learn the 4 Things You Need to Know if You Have Been Hurt in a Car Wreck.'
ads.iterate: Video version: '3 things to know before you talk to their insurance'.

ads.breakdown: TopDog Law: simple emoji hook 'Injured in a Car Accident? 🚗💥🚙' running as 18 copies since 9/1, so it's being scaled hard.
Eric Roy (Las Vegas): personality firm that sells the service: 'case managers every 2 weeks, Eric himself every 40 days'.
Woman at home, selfie UGC: '$1,756 for a move from Florida to California? That's not a quote. That's a trap.' Calls out lowball web quotes that jump on move day.
ads.iterate: 'Why cheap quotes double on move day' UGC — positions an honest full-service price as the safe choice.

ads.breakdown: Truck render with 'Moving Cost Calculator — ENTER ZIP, VIEW RATES'. Copy: 'as Low as $1,589 — we'll do the heavy lifting so you won't need a chiropractor'. Running since May 2025.
ads.iterate: Calculator-style static into our quiz funnel, with realistic price ranges.

ads.breakdown: Budget Van Lines: 'WHAT DOES IT COST TO MOVE?' plus 'most popular moving cost calculator — trusted by over 6.8 million'. Truck photo + VIEW RATES button. Running since Jan 2025.
ads.iterate: 'What does it cost to move out of state?' calculator static with a real range.

ads.breakdown: Budget Van Lines: 'LONG DISTANCE MOVING — most used moving site in the US' with route prices (CA→NY $1,999, PA→OH $1,460, TX→IL $1,790) and 'Enter ZIP and view your rates'. 4 copies running.
ads.iterate: Route-price static for our top lanes — but with honest full-service prices, not bait prices.

ads.breakdown: Two Movers: truck with route price tags (Dallas→Chicago $1,078, Phoenix→Seattle $1,623, Fargo→Miami $2,149) and 'VIEW YOUR RATES'. Many near-identical versions running.
Quote Runner: plain 'Are you Moving Soon? I NEED QUOTES' button graphic. Copy: 'Long distance movers from $999, enter ZIP'. Running since July 2019.
ads.iterate: Ultra-simple text static test (TCC's black-text-on-white static is its top performer).

ads.breakdown: Howards Van Line: real family photo + checklist (free estimates, licensed & insured, on-time) — 'Family owned, 60 years', 'NOT a broker', 'Call for $500 OFF'.
ads.iterate: 'Not a broker — your move stays with one operator' trust static (the dedicated-operator point).

ads.breakdown: America's Moving: 'Moving out of state? Don't get scammed!' with truck, 'AVOID SUMMER RATES — starting at $1495'.
Accurate Van Lines: route prices on a truck (NYC→LA $1,842) + big phone number. Copy: 'Moving out of state is expensive. Getting scammed makes it worse.'
Next Stop Relocation: real photo of a fully packed truck. Copy leads with 'Veteran-Owned, full-service moving company'.
ads.iterate: Veterans are an untapped persona for us — a military/PCS family move angle.

ads.breakdown: New Start: animated route-price grid ('California→Texas $1,699 — Most Popular!', 'NY→CA $1,949'), then 'Get quote'.
ads.iterate: Animated 'popular routes' grid — real lanes, realistic starting prices.

ads.breakdown: Brightside: branded truck driving through a suburb, captions 'Moving Across States?'. Copy lists routes: 'Florida→New York from $1,799. California→Texas from $1,899…'
Brightside: same truck b-roll, 'SAVE UP TO 20% — long-distance routes from $1,799'.
Mayzlin Relocation: semi truck in a palm-tree neighborhood, captions + 'Example routes' in copy. Long-distance from $1,899.
Adams Van Lines: real crew loading boxes up a ramp, 'LONG DISTANCE MOVING MADE SIMPLE'. Copy: no stress, no surprise charges, movers who show up on time.
ads.iterate: Real VAM crew footage with 'no surprise charges on move day'.

ads.breakdown: Adams Van Lines: 'The pod is sitting in your driveway. And your heavy furniture is still upstairs.' Full-service vs portable-container angle.
ads.iterate: Container-vs-full-service ad: 'you still have to load it yourself' — strong fit for VAM's full-service move.

ads.breakdown: AAA Movers: local TV personality (Jason Matheson) endorsement; text hook 'Have you used a different moving company before?' Running since July 2025.
ads.iterate: 'Have you used a different moving company before?' switcher hook with a real VAM customer.

ads.breakdown: UltaMovers: crew member selfie at the truck. 'Most movers tell you they're careful. We'd rather just show you. Our average crew member has completed over 600 residential moves.'
ads.iterate: Crew-member selfie UGC with one real proof number (moves completed, years driving).

ads.breakdown: Sparrow Moving: 'If your kids ask "Where's my stuff?" after moving — you'll love this.' Boxes in a new home, family unpacking service.
ads.iterate: Family persona: 'the first night in the new house' — beds made, kids' rooms set up.

ads.advertiser: Pink Zebra Moving of Round Rock TX
ads.breakdown: Pink Zebra: kinetic 3D text ('trusting strangers with…') over people and the brand mascot. Lists the fears: movers showing up late, damaged furniture, hidden fees.
ads.iterate: Humor/pattern-interrupt test — the Avatar Dancing lesson from Case Source may carry over.

ads.breakdown: Movingyourself: older man selfie UGC, 'State to state cheap moving option.' You load, we drive. 'America's lowest-cost long distance'.
ads.iterate: Older presenter talking to seniors/downsizers — another untapped persona for us.

ads.breakdown: Moving Solutions: female creator in a room full of boxes, '#ad Planning a move out of state? Skip the stress and get a quote you can actually trust.' 1:05.
ads.iterate: Creator/partnership-style UGC (#ad) — the playbook's partnership-ads gap.

ads.breakdown: HireAHelper: couple carrying boxes in an empty home, '$1,000 service guarantee when you book'.
X Van Lines: 'BEFORE' furniture shot — before/after of how items arrive. 6 copies running, so they're scaling it.
ads.iterate: Before/after 'how your furniture arrives' — wrapped vs unwrapped.
